title: Is AI capable of teaching/creating a multiplayer game?
author: q_OwO_p
selftext:
Hello, I wanted to ask is AI able to help with creating a game with multiplayer, more specifically I mean steam multiplayer, I think it’s called steamworks?

I plan to use Love2D for my engine because I know some LUA coding somewhat and it seems lightweight and simple for the type of game I want to make (turn-based card game), but I know nothing about networking or how to make do multiplayer so I was hoping to lean on an AI to teach me and do all the multiplayer functionality for me.

And in case somebody has made a multiplayer game using AI on here, how did it go? Did the AI do the heavy lifting or did you have to do all the multiplayer functionality yourself? And what AI did you use?

comments.author: BillBangkok
comments.body:
Sure, it can help, but don’t expect to rely on it 100%. You still need to learn how to build multiplayer systems along the way while using AI, because some of the problems you’ll face will be related to architecture. 

Also, using models like Claude Opus or Gemini Pro 3 can help reduce headaches when developing with AI.

comments.author: MediocreHelicopter19
comments.body: It can teach you, but it will take you a lot of time if you don't know anything. AI is a great teacher; still, if you need a 5-year degree, with a good teacher, you will need 5 years to learn it.
